title: @inth/nextjs: Next.js cookie banner and cookie consent management
description: Next.js cookie banner, consent dialog, and preference center for the App Router and Pages Router. The server resolves each visitor's consent policy, such as GDPR opt-in in the EU, and renders the banner in the first HTML. Use headless hooks for your own UI.
features: Works with Next.js 15 and 16, on the App Router and the Pages Router
On dynamic pages, the server resolves each visitor's policy and sends it in the same response. Await `resolveConsent()` to put the banner in the first HTML
Your policy downloads at build time with `withConsentManifest`, so rendering never waits on the consent backend
Prebuilt cookie banner, consent dialog, and preference center with a theme system
Headless hooks for a fully custom design
Analytics, ads, and pixels follow each visitor's choice through @inth/integrations: Google Tag Manager, Google Consent Mode v2, GA4, Meta Pixel, PostHog, and more
IAB TCF 2.4 banner, dialog, and hooks through the @inth/react/iab subpath
prerequisites: An [Inth project](https://inth.com) (free sign-up), or `testing()` for development and tests
manualInstallation: Then add the prebuilt stylesheet to your app-level CSS entry point:
usage: Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_INTH_PROJECT_URL` to your Inth project URL in `.env`
Wrap `next.config.ts` in `withConsentManifest`, which downloads your policy at build time and finds `inth.config.ts`

```ts
// next.config.ts
import { withConsentManifest } from '@inth/nextjs/build'
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig = {} satisfies NextConfig

export default withConsentManifest(nextConfig)
```
Export the config from `inth.config.ts` at the project root
Render `InthProvider` with `ConsentBanner` and `ConsentDialog` in the root layout, and pass it `resolveConsent()`
For the full setup, see the [Next.js quickstart](https://inth.com/docs/frameworks/next/quickstart)
